name: fill-from-the-segment-wrap-at-modulo-four-and-eight
rationale: Settles the owed Metal reading of simd_shuffle_and_fill_{down,up} at modulo 4 and 8 (/; the engine ports the old engine's segment rule). One threadgroup of 64 threads, two full simdgroups (lanes t & 31). Each thread shuffles data t with fill t + 1000 eight ways (down 1 and 3 at modulo 4, up 1 and 3 at modulo 4, down 3 and 6 at modulo 8, up 2 and 7 at modulo 8, all constant operands in the AIR) and writes them to out[8t .. 8t + 8). Under the documented rule a lane l = lane % modulo reads data t +/- delta while that stays in its segment, else the fill of the lane the shift wraps to inside the segment (t + delta - modulo + 1000 down, t - delta + modulo + 1000 up), so every word names its source lane and operand (data < 64, fill >= 1000): a segment of the wrong width, a wrap to the neighbouring segment or simdgroup, or data where fill is due is visible in the word. Every word is below 1100 and differs from the 0xAB poison. No thread diverges and the AIR has no loop.

name: nan-model-float-flush-at-the-tininess-boundary
rationale: Whether Metal flushes a float result that is below 2^-126 before rounding but rounds to 2^-126, in its compile without fast math. Lane i reads (a, b, c, n), n an int, and writes 8 words: a * b, a / b, fma(a, b, c), a * b + c, ldexp(a, n), -(a * b), -(a / b), and fma(-a, b, -c). Lanes: multiply and fused multiply-add, 48 and 40 whose exact result lies in [2^-126 (1 - 2^-25), 2^-126), tiny before rounding only, and 48 and 40 in [2^-126 (1 - 2^-24), 2^-126 (1 - 2^-25)), tiny after rounding as well, where the gradual-underflow result still rounds to 2^-126, with 16 controls near 2^-126 each; division at 2^-126 - 2^-150 by a power of two (the only quotient of floats in either range) and its neighbour, with 16 controls; and 16 ldexp lanes at 2^-126 (1 - 2^-24) and below; half of each group negated. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: helper-thread-alone-after-a-terminating-discard
rationale: MSL 2.2, whose discard terminates. Drawn over a 7x5 target: its last column and row are quads the target cuts, whose lanes past the target Metal runs as helpers. The pixels with (x + y) mod 3 == 0 discard and hold the target's initial bytes. A live pixel returns q | s << 1, its own answers, which are 0, and 7 in the other three words: nothing after the discard reads another lane.

name: helper-threads-after-a-terminating-discard
rationale: MSL 2.2, whose discard terminates. Drawn over a 7x5 target: its last column and row are quads the target cuts, whose lanes past the target Metal runs as helpers. The pixels with (x + y) mod 3 == 0 discard, which keeps each running as a helper on Metal as at MSL 2.3; every quad keeps two or three live pixels, so the discarded pixels hold the target's initial bytes and the live ones report them. After the discard, a pixel returns q | s << 1 (its quad_is_helper_thread and simd_is_helper_thread), its quad's quad_ballot of q and of s, and quad_active_threads_mask: helpers are active lanes of their quad, so the mask is 15, and the ballots name the quad's helpers.

name: convert-integers-across-every-width
rationale: Twenty-three uncovered air.convert.* families in one kernel, plus five that come free with them: air.convert.u.v4i16.u.v4i1 (2 case-less corpus sources), air.convert.u.v4i16.f.v4f16 (2), air.convert.u.v3i16.u.v3i8 (2), air.convert.s.v2i32.s.v2i8 (2), air.convert.s.v2i16.s.v2i32 (2), air.convert.f.v4f16.u.v4i16 (2) and seventeen more at one source each -- 29 sources. A width conversion has exactly two ways to be wrong and both are silent: it can sign-extend where it should zero-extend, and it can keep bits it should have dropped. Every input is chosen so both show. The narrowing sources overflow their destination on purpose -- t * 300 - 500 and -t * 70000 + 5 do not fit in 8 or 16 bits, so char4(i4) and short4(i4) must drop the high bits rather than clamp, and the surviving low bits differ per thread. Half the lanes are negative: t - 3 is negative for the first three threads and -t * 70000 for all but the first, so a widening that zero-extended a signed source, or a narrowing read back as signed where the symbol says unsigned, lands four orders of magnitude away rather than at a plausible neighbour. u4.w is 4294967040 + t, which is negative as an int32 and enormous as a uint32 -- the same disagreement at the other end, and its truncation to 65280 + t is the evidence the high bits went. Both signednesses of the same byte pattern are asked side by side: uchar4(i4) and char4(i4) must produce identical bytes under different symbols, and int4(uchar4(u4)) against int4(c4) separates zero- from sign-extension on the same width pair. The halves are all non-negative with a fraction of 3/4 or 1/2, so the float-to-integer direction truncates toward zero rather than rounding and the answer moves by one if it rounds. The integer-to-half direction is asked where it is exact: u4 masked to 16 bits gives 0, 300..2100 in steps of 300, 4464..31248 in steps of 4464 and 65280, and every one of those is a whole multiple of its binade's half spacing, so the whole vector is representable and a mismatch is a lowering difference rather than a rounding one. The 64-bit results are written as two 32-bit words each, low first, so a conversion that produced the right low word and the wrong sign extension is still visible; ulong4(u4) and ulong4(i4) are asked on the same lanes for exactly that. Every store is straight-line, so the module is loop-free.

name: constant-half4-magenta-target-zero
rationale: The fragment writes literal half4 magenta to location zero and position depth to location four; this case independently selects the constant output while binding both sparse attachments.

name: fragment-position-depth-target-four
rationale: The fragment writes literal half4 magenta to location zero and its position z lane to location four; this case independently selects the sparse depth-as-color output while binding both attachments.

name: tile-threads-16x16-in-a-16x16-tile-take-their-places
rationale: One 16x16 tile of an r32_float attachment (pixels y*16+x) run by a 16x16 threadgroup: each thread records, at its thread_index_in_threadgroup, its thread_position_in_threadgroup, lane, and simdgroup and the position of its simdgroup's first lane (simd_broadcast_first), so the observation is the tile dispatch's layout of its threads: thread indices over 2x2 quads in row-major order, simdgroups of 8x4 positions.

name: tile-threads-16x16-in-a-32x32-tile-take-their-places
rationale: One 32x32 tile of an r32_float attachment (pixels y*32+x) run by a 16x16 threadgroup: each thread records, at its thread_index_in_threadgroup, its thread_position_in_threadgroup, lane, and simdgroup and the position of its simdgroup's first lane (simd_broadcast_first), so the observation is the tile dispatch's layout of its threads: thread indices over 2x2 quads in row-major order, simdgroups of 8x4 positions.

rationale: One 16x16 tile of an r32_float attachment (pixels y*16+x) run by a 4x4 threadgroup: each thread records, at its thread_index_in_threadgroup, its thread_position_in_threadgroup, lane, and simdgroup and the position of its simdgroup's first lane (simd_broadcast_first), so the observation is the tile dispatch's layout of its threads: thread indices over 2x2 quads in row-major order, simdgroups of 8x4 positions.

rationale: One 16x16 tile of an r32_float attachment (pixels y*16+x) run by a 8x8 threadgroup: each thread records, at its thread_index_in_threadgroup, its thread_position_in_threadgroup, lane, and simdgroup and the position of its simdgroup's first lane (simd_broadcast_first), so the observation is the tile dispatch's layout of its threads: thread indices over 2x2 quads in row-major order, simdgroups of 8x4 positions.

name: premultiply-gamma-through-short-texture-coordinates
rationale: air.read_texture_2d.i16.v4f16 and air.write_texture_2d.i16.v4f16 address a texture through SHORT coordinates rather than the int coordinates every other authored texture case uses, and this entry drives both against one read_write binding in place, once per thread. It premultiplies alpha in gamma space, pow(alpha * pow(rgb, 2.2), 1/2.2). Every channel is authored 0.0 or 1.0 so both powers are exact on any implementation and the case measures the coordinate ABI rather than transcendental precision: the four texels (1,1,1,1), (0,0,0,1), (1,0,1,0) and (0,1,0,1) must become (1,1,1,1), (0,0,0,1), (0,0,0,0) and (0,1,0,1), four distinct values, so a coordinate that were widened or ordered wrongly would land a thread on another texel and change the captured 2x2 region.

name: linked-single-complex-transpose-write
rationale: One dispatched invocation addresses one NDArray element. The reference-size and coordinate-mapping constants bound every dimension and stride to one; the linked prefix returns an exact nonzero value, the linked postfix writes it, and both callbacks are loop-free. Transpose variants use one initialized lane and the exact reflected dynamic threadgroup allocation.

name: constant-half4-render-target
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns a constant half4 to attachment zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned RGBA16Float pixel.

name: cube-major-axis-ties-at-5x5
rationale: Which face and texel Metal reads along a cube direction whose components tie for the largest magnitude, or lie at either end of the float range, on an rgba32_float cube of 5x5 faces whose texel (i, j) of face f holds (f + 1, i + 1, j + 1, 0). Lane i samples dir[i] through a nearest clamp-to-edge sampler: every pair of tied axes in all four sign combinations with the third component 0, +-0.25 or +-0.885 times the magnitude, and every triple tie in all eight, at magnitudes 1, 0.885, 0.5 and 3; at magnitude 1 each tied component one ulp larger as a control; and (-1, -0.885, -1), case 914ba505's lane 239; then directions below the normal range, which Metal reads with each subnormal component zero and a direction left zero at face +x's texel (0, 0): zero in all eight signs, subnormal on one, two, or three axes at magnitudes 2^-149, 2^-140, 2^-127 and the largest subnormal; and directions at both ends of the normal range, where Metal reads a face coordinate's component below 2^-125 as zero, and every one as zero past a major magnitude of 2^126: minors of 2^-126, 1.5 * 2^-126 and subnormal ones beside majors of 2^-125 and 2^-120, ties at 2^-125, 2^-124, the float above 2^-126, 2^-100, 1e-30, 2^100, 2^127 and the largest float, and 2^125 beside 2^126. It also gathers the red, green and blue components at gdir[i], the same direction where the 2x2 block stays off the cube's corners (a corner texel is the device's choice in Vulkan), else another such lane.

name: cube-major-axis-ties-at-8x8
rationale: Which face and texel Metal reads along a cube direction whose components tie for the largest magnitude, or lie at either end of the float range, on an rgba32_float cube of 8x8 faces whose texel (i, j) of face f holds (f + 1, i + 1, j + 1, 0). Lane i samples dir[i] through a nearest clamp-to-edge sampler: every pair of tied axes in all four sign combinations with the third component 0, +-0.25 or +-0.885 times the magnitude, and every triple tie in all eight, at magnitudes 1, 0.885, 0.5 and 3; at magnitude 1 each tied component one ulp larger as a control; and (-1, -0.885, -1), case 914ba505's lane 239; then directions below the normal range, which Metal reads with each subnormal component zero and a direction left zero at face +x's texel (0, 0): zero in all eight signs, subnormal on one, two, or three axes at magnitudes 2^-149, 2^-140, 2^-127 and the largest subnormal; and directions at both ends of the normal range, where Metal reads a face coordinate's component below 2^-125 as zero, and every one as zero past a major magnitude of 2^126: minors of 2^-126, 1.5 * 2^-126 and subnormal ones beside majors of 2^-125 and 2^-120, ties at 2^-125, 2^-124, the float above 2^-126, 2^-100, 1e-30, 2^100, 2^127 and the largest float, and 2^125 beside 2^126. It also gathers the red, green and blue components at gdir[i], the same direction where the 2x2 block stays off the cube's corners (a corner texel is the device's choice in Vulkan), else another such lane.

name: average-three-channels-left-to-right-before-widening
rationale: The first three channels take the rebalancing branch, which collapses the bounds to 10 and 23 and replaces the average by the mean of the three supplied averages -- a three-term sum the shader spells left to right and then divides by three, and neither the adds nor the divide carries permission to reassociate or to use a reciprocal. The three averages are chosen so grouping the sum the other way lands on a different float, and the second stage widens that difference by four and a half before the upper bound is stored, while the lower bound clamps and says so. The fourth channel keeps its own average and rides a separate, exactly representable widening, so it pins the untouched lane.

name: evaluate-one-uniform-member-from-two-call-sites
rationale: A `constant Params&` whose first member is handed to a NOINLINE helper from TWO call sites. Metal's `constant` space carries whole uniform structs, so a helper that takes one member of one is routinely called again -- and only one byte cursor per callee parameter can be recorded, so the emitter used to refuse the second call site's cursor by refusing every callee with more than one call site. Both call sites here name the same member, so no cursor can conflict, but the helper still read its whole coefficient struct as zero: ten loads folded to `OpConstantNull` with spirv-val happy. The helper is two blocks on purpose -- a one-block leaf is inlined before the call path is ever reached. Buffer 0 holds a = (1, 2, 3, 4), then a decoy b = (1000, 2000, 3000, 4000), then scale = 2. The helper evaluates 4x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x + 1 at x = gid, and odd threads add its value at gid + 1, so both call sites are live and the second one is the one the old gate refused. Every coefficient, every power of an integer gid up to 8, and every partial sum is an exact binary32 integer below 2^24, so fast-math reassociation and fma contraction cannot move the answer: (2, 118, 98, 910, 626, 3142, 1970, 7582). The three failure modes are all separated. Coefficients read as zero give all zeros; the decoy member read instead gives values a thousand times larger; a cursor dropped only on the second call site leaves the four ODD lanes short.

name: bicubic-edges-of-random-texels-in-a-12x10-rgba16-float
rationale: Metal's filter::bicubic at the edges of a 12x10 rgba16_float texture of random texels under each address mode the translation lowers, and with pixel coordinates: the lanes of bicubic-address-modes-at-the-edges-of-a-<size>-<format> without its mirrored_repeat sampler, so that a Vulkan candidate runs every sampler. The texels are seeded random values (numpy default_rng(11); unorm codes 0-255, float values uniform in [-1, 2) at the format's precision), so a sample's channels are sums of sixteen weighted texels and the format's clamp or rounding, and a tap outside the texture shows its border. Each lane reads (u, v, x, y) from buffer 0: a pixel-space point x, y and the same point normalized, u = x / width and v = y / height as binary32 (exact for a power-of-two extent; for 12x10 the rounded quotient). Twenty x positions from 2.25 texels outside the left edge to 2.25 outside the right one, on two rows; twenty y positions likewise on the middle column; four outside corners. Each lane writes the samples of six bicubic samplers to out[6i..6i+5] of buffer 1: normalized clamp_to_edge, clamp_to_zero, clamp_to_border with an opaque white border, and repeat, and pixel-coordinate clamp_to_edge and clamp_to_zero. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-edges-of-random-texels-in-a-12x10-rgba32-float
rationale: Metal's filter::bicubic at the edges of a 12x10 rgba32_float texture of random texels under each address mode the translation lowers, and with pixel coordinates: the lanes of bicubic-address-modes-at-the-edges-of-a-<size>-<format> without its mirrored_repeat sampler, so that a Vulkan candidate runs every sampler. The texels are seeded random values (numpy default_rng(13); unorm codes 0-255, float values uniform in [-1, 2) at the format's precision), so a sample's channels are sums of sixteen weighted texels and the format's clamp or rounding, and a tap outside the texture shows its border. Each lane reads (u, v, x, y) from buffer 0: a pixel-space point x, y and the same point normalized, u = x / width and v = y / height as binary32 (exact for a power-of-two extent; for 12x10 the rounded quotient). Twenty x positions from 2.25 texels outside the left edge to 2.25 outside the right one, on two rows; twenty y positions likewise on the middle column; four outside corners. Each lane writes the samples of six bicubic samplers to out[6i..6i+5] of buffer 1: normalized clamp_to_edge, clamp_to_zero, clamp_to_border with an opaque white border, and repeat, and pixel-coordinate clamp_to_edge and clamp_to_zero. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-edges-of-random-texels-in-a-16x16-r8-unorm
rationale: Metal's filter::bicubic at the edges of a 16x16 r8_unorm texture of random texels under each address mode the translation lowers, and with pixel coordinates: the lanes of bicubic-address-modes-at-the-edges-of-a-<size>-<format> without its mirrored_repeat sampler, so that a Vulkan candidate runs every sampler. The texels are seeded random values (numpy default_rng(12); unorm codes 0-255, float values uniform in [-1, 2) at the format's precision), so a sample's channels are sums of sixteen weighted texels and the format's clamp or rounding, and a tap outside the texture shows its border. Each lane reads (u, v, x, y) from buffer 0: a pixel-space point x, y and the same point normalized, u = x / width and v = y / height as binary32 (exact for a power-of-two extent; for 16x16 the rounded quotient). Twenty x positions from 2.25 texels outside the left edge to 2.25 outside the right one, on two rows; twenty y positions likewise on the middle column; four outside corners. Each lane writes the samples of six bicubic samplers to out[6i..6i+5] of buffer 1: normalized clamp_to_edge, clamp_to_zero, clamp_to_border with an opaque white border, and repeat, and pixel-coordinate clamp_to_edge and clamp_to_zero. The AIR has no loop.

name: fixed-array-eight-simdgroup-maximum
rationale: One complete 256-thread workgroup forms exactly eight 32-lane SIMD groups, so every shared reduction slot is initialized before the barrier. The kernel structurally selects element zero of the fixed texture array; its pixel-coordinate clamp-to-edge sampler makes every gather return uint 7, and thread zero writes the exact uint4 maximum.

name: constant-float2-render-target
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns float2 zero at color location one; one full-coverage fragment must replace the exact eight-byte poisoned RG32Float pixel.

name: constant-half4-magenta-target-zero
rationale: The fragment writes literal half4 (1,0,1,1) to color location zero and fragment-position depth to color location four; this case selects the independently observable constant output while binding both sparse attachments.

name: fragment-position-depth-target-four
rationale: The fragment writes literal half4 magenta to color location zero and its position z lane to color location four; this case independently selects the sparse R32Float depth-as-color output while binding both attachments.

name: accumulate-four-weighted-coefficients-as-one-fused-step
rationale: The kernel is one multiply feeding one add, so nothing else can move the result and the four lanes are independent. The module is compiled air.compile.fast_math_enable and both operations carry the fast flag, which lets the pair be contracted into a fused multiply-add. All four coefficient/accumulator pairs are chosen so the fused answer and the separately rounded one land on different floats, so the sixteen observed bytes say which of the two the pipeline performed.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-eight
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 8 and receives exact float4 zero from all seven linked _uber_clear bodies. A ten-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; the final selector reads register 2 and writes exact zero to the poisoned primary texel.

name: linked-single-unit-reduce-multiple-passes-axes-add
rationale: One invocation reduces one float element along axis zero. Every four-lane reduction extent, per-thread count, per-threadgroup count, source and destination bound, broadcast extent, and NDArray size and stride is one, so all loops are bounded by the single authored element.

name: bicubic-impulse-weights-per-bound-format
rationale: Which filter Metal's filter::bicubic applies to each bound pixel format, read as weights. an impulse case returned two linear weights on an rgba32_float texture, while a corpus case on rgba16_float returned Catmull-Rom weights, so the filter may depend on the format bound. Ten 16x16 textures are sampled through one clamp-to-edge, normalized bicubic sampler in the corpus's form (an implicit sample, the base level in a kernel): slots 0-7 bind r8_unorm, rgba8_unorm, r16_float, rg16_float, rgba16_float, r32_float, rg32_float and rgba32_float, slots 8 and 9 are half textures binding rgba16_float and rgba8_unorm. Every texture holds the same impulses: channel c of texel (x, y) is 1 where (x - y - c) mod 4 == 0 and 0 elsewhere (one-channel formats keep channel 0), so at a vertical fraction of zero a sample returns, in channel c, the weight of the one horizontal tap whose column is congruent to y + c mod 4. Lanes 0-127 sweep 32 horizontal fractions (k/16, then 1/4096, 1/1024, 1/512, 3/1024, 1/256, 3/512, 1/128, 9/512, 0.1, 1/3, 127/256, 255/512, 257/512, 129/256, 255/256, 4095/4096) at base texel 4 over rows 4-7, so the four rows read the four taps; lanes 128-191 do the same vertically at k/16; lanes 192-223 take both axes fractional ((2j+1)/64, (63-2j)/64); lanes 224-255 put the footprint across each edge. Coordinates are binary32 normalized values from buffer 0 (exact except 0.1 and 1/3, whose sampled fraction is that of the rounded coordinate); lane i writes its ten samples to out[10i..10i+9] of buffer 1, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bicubic-of-random-texels-per-bound-format
rationale: The precision of Metal's filter::bicubic per bound pixel format: the same ten slots and 256 lane coordinates as bicubic-impulse-weights-per-bound-format, but every texture holds seeded pseudo-random texels (unorm8 formats random bytes, float formats values uniform in [-1, 2) rounded to the format; the half slots repeat the rgba16_float and rgba8_unorm data of slots 4 and 1), so each sample is a weighted sum whose rounding shows the arithmetic the filter does. A Metal reading: the weights and their quantization come from the impulse case, and this case measures how far Metal's sums are from an exact evaluation of them. The AIR has no loop.

name: read-and-write-a-subword-vector-through-a-word-pointer
rationale: A subword vector read from, and written back through, a WORD pointer -- the *(device ushort2*) reinterpret Metal code writes whenever it treats a uint buffer as pairs of halves. The SPIR-V pointer keeps its declared uint pointee, so both directions are equal-width reinterprets of the VALUE and are the same two instructions in mirror image: the load is OpLoad of the word plus OpBitcast up to ushort2, the store is OpBitcast down to the word plus OpStore. The emitter must therefore accept the same pointee/object pairs on both sides; a store arm narrower than the load arm refuses to write back what the load just read. in[i] packs two DIFFERENT halves, 0x0100+i low and 0x0200+i high, so a swapped lane pair is visible as a value and not just as a width. The first two rows extract each half through ordinary word stores, which pins which half is which; the third row is the reinterpret store itself, writing the halves back SWAPPED as one word. The fourth row is never written and must still hold its 0xCD fill: a store that took the narrowing path would leave half of out[16+i] at the fill byte, and a store that overshot its word would land in row three. Each lane writes one slot no other lane touches, so there is no race.

name: vertex-position-depth-zero
rationale: The vertex entry preserves authored x/y, forces clip-space z to zero and w to one, and the typed position observer captures the resulting full-coverage triangle.

name: fast-trig-across-the-whole-evaluated-range
rationale:
fast::sin and fast::cos on float3 and on a scalar, at the arguments that separate Metal's own reduction from a hand-rolled one. Six of the eight are the correctly rounded float32 sine or cosine of the argument -- derived here in float64 and rounded once, 0 ULP against the observation at every one -- and the remaining two are the flush.

The first lane is the point of the case. This translator used to reduce the argument itself, x - trunc(x / 2pi) * 2pi, before handing it to the trig call. That expression rounds twice, so the residue it produces carries the absolute error of a number the size of x rather than of the residue, and at x = 100 the answer came back 38 ULP from Metal's. Metal reduces more carefully than that, and so does the MSL sin the emitted GLSL call becomes, so the reduction was pure loss; it is gone, and this lane is what says so. The 1e6 lanes, in both signs, are two decades further out and would move further still.

The third lane of each vector is 6588397.5, which is float(pi/2) times 2^22 -- the largest magnitude the hardware still evaluates, bisected on this repository's reference GPU. The two scalars are the very next float in each direction, 6588398 and its negative, where both functions answer exactly zero. A lowering that dropped the flush would return an ordinary sine there instead of zero, and one that flushed a binade early would return zero for the vector's third lane.

name: math-library-accuracy-at-1024-operand-pairs-without-fast-math
rationale: Each of 1024 threads writes 32 words for its (x, y), compiled without fast math (-fno-fast-math; MSL Table 8.1; air.<name>.f32): (sin x, cos x, tan x, sincos's sine), (sincos's cosine, asin x, acos x, atan x), (atan2(y, x), sinh x, cosh x, tanh x), (asinh x, acosh x, atanh x, exp x), (exp2 x, exp10 x, log x, log2 x), (log10 x, pow(x, y), powr(x, y), sqrt x), (rsqrt x, fmod(x, y), sinpi x, cospi x), and (tanpi x, x / y, atan2(x, y), y). Operands, 1,024 (x, y) float pairs in eight sections: 32 special pairs (both zeros, the smallest and largest denormals, the smallest normal, +-1, +-0.5, +-2, both infinities, a NaN, both largest finites, +-pi, +-pi/2, the neighbours of 1, Metal's fast trig flush point float(pi/2) * 2^22 and its neighbour, the exp limits); 192 in [-1, 1] (uniform, the eight floats below each of +-1, the powers 2^-1 to 2^-24, small magnitudes down to 2^-126); 128 at the float nearest k * pi/2 and its two neighbours for k = 1 to 32, and at 32 large k up to 2^126; 256 log-uniform over every binade from 2^-126 to 2^127, alternating signs; 128 in [0.5, 2] and at the 16 floats on each side of 1 and 1 +- 2^-k; 96 at the exponentials' edges and over [-104, 89]; 64 over the hyperbolics' ranges ([-20, 20], [-90, 90], [1, 1e30]); 64 pow pairs (wide exponents, results at the range's edges, exact powers and roots); and 64 trig arguments in [-1e4, 1e4] and at the flush point's neighbours and powers of two. y is an exponent, a divisor, or atan2's other operand, by section. Inputs generated deterministically (seed 0x7A4E297). Question: for each function, how far Metal's answer and each device's are from the exact value, against Apple's stated bound, and what Metal answers where Apple states none.

name: fused-multiply-add-rounding-and-fmuladd-without-fast-math
rationale: Each of 1024 threads computes fma(a, b, c) and a * b + c on one float triple and one half triple, and the lone float product a * w. The float triples: the three lanes of 52343cc4 and their negations (the exact product minus its rounding), exact cancellations and signed zeros, infinities and NaNs, products past the largest float that the addend brings back, denormal operands, products, and sums, 96 triples whose exact sum lies within 2^-60 of a float midpoint with the addend dominant and 96 with the product dominant (so an f64 sum rounded to float rounds twice and goes the wrong way: the hazard an f64 emulation must remove with round-to-odd), 160 where one rounding and two differ, and random triples. The half triples: 300 whose exact sum rounded to float first lands on a half midpoint (a half fma computed as a float fma and rounded to half goes the wrong way), 200 where one half rounding and two differ, the special values, and random triples. Compiled without fast math: fma is air.fma and a * b + c is llvm.fmuladd (fused or not, as the implementation chooses). Questions: is Metal's fma correctly rounded without fast math too, does Metal fuse llvm.fmuladd, and does it flush a denormal float product or keep it.

name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage
rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.

name: three-instances-read-by-thread-zero
rationale: The C1 row that only queries an instance acceleration structure's count: thread 0 stores get_instance_count() of a structure the oracle builds with three instances and thread 1 stores nothing, so the output is 3. On profiles without ray queries the Vulkan candidate reads the count the binder pushes from the case's structure.
